clue.text: Country girl on river

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A country girl perched on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'girl on river' just means the girl is joined to the river letter; here the river comes first, giving R+WANDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a nation in east-central Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Rebuke fish salesman initially

indicators.note: initially says this part comes at the start, placed in front rather than after as the clue's word order suggests

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fishmonger gets a telling-off at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it tells you to put the salesman at the start, before the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to rebuke them, expressing disapproval or disappointment.

clue.text: Dog exhibited by porter

blocks.note: something aired has been shown in public
porter is a dark beer, so a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A dog put on show by a hotel porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' suggests a doorman, but it is the dark beer; 'by' sets the beer beside the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Nightclub party gatecrashed by one self-catering

indicators.note: a gatecrasher gets inside uninvited, so the next words end up within the first

blocks.note: a do is a party
I is the Roman numeral for one
SC is the abbreviation for self-catering in holiday listings

explanation.surface: A club night ruined by a holidaymaker from a self-catering flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a club or event where people dance to recorded music, so a kind of nightclub.

clue.text: Careless fielders keep dropping Leicestershire's opener

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so a letter is removed from the word before it
an opener is what starts things off, so only the first letter of the county is wanted

blocks.note: slips are close catching fielders in cricket, standing beside the wicketkeeper
to keep is to hold
the opening letter of the county name

explanation.surface: Sloppy fielders keep putting down catches off Leicestershire's opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicestershire is an English county with a cricket team, and 'opener' reads as its opening batsman; really it is just its first letter, removed from HOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod is a synonym for careless: done without proper attention or tidiness.

clue.text: Film entailed devil reforming

indicators.note: reforming means forming again, so the letters before it are shaped into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A film that involved a devil mending its ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Live and Let Die is a 1973 James Bond movie, Roger Moore's first, so an example of a film.

clue.text: Carnivore in tree caught by one animal doctor

blocks.note: a palm is a tree
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral for one
a vet treats animals

explanation.surface: A meat-eater up a tree is captured by a veterinarian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'caught by' suggest containers, but every piece is simply laid end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm civet is a small tree-dwelling mammal of Asia and Africa, classed among carnivores.

clue.text: Robin? That is a crow

blocks.note: Robin Hood, the legendary outlaw
first half of the abbreviation for 'that is', from Latin id est
second half of the 'that is' abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bird is a robin and is told it is a crow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' gives IE, short for Latin id est; the bare 'a crow' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoodie is a colloquial name for the hooded crow, a grey-and-black crow of northern Britain.

clue.text: Stop in untidy side street

indicators.note: untidy means messed up and out of order, so the letters that follow are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Pulling up in a messy back street.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to stop or cease doing something, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Capital English chronicler

blocks.note: first meaning: the capital city of France
second meaning: Matthew ..., a 13th-century Benedictine monk at St Albans who wrote chronicles

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like one description, but it splits into a city and a medieval historian who share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the French capital city, and Matthew Paris was a medieval English monk and historian.

clue.text: Buildings pal with vision designed

indicators.note: something designed has been planned and laid out afresh, so the letters before it are arranged anew

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some structures created by a friend with an artistic vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavilions are buildings, typically ornamental or for sports spectators, such as at a cricket ground.

clue.text: Government leader to brief clergyman

blocks.note: to prime someone is to brief them in advance
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A head of government is to give instructions to a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: The prime minister heads the government in a parliamentary system such as Britain's.

clue.text: Strange old theologian

blocks.note: O is a common abbreviation for old
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree

explanation.surface: A peculiar elderly scholar of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and strange are synonyms, both meaning unusual or peculiar.

clue.text: Crude oil charge is criminal, but it's good for these governments

indicators.note: crude means raw or unrefined, so the letters that follow are taken in a rough jumbled state
criminal suggests something bent and twisted, backing up the call to rearrange the letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Overcharging for crude oil is a crime, though it suits regimes run by a wealthy few.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the tail of the clue, which also comments on the surface: high oil prices enrich oil states run by small elites.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchies are states ruled by a small, often wealthy group, which is the kind of government meant.

clue.text: Bird caught right away from port

indicators.note: 'away from' means taken off, so the named letter leaves the word that follows

blocks.note: to be collared is to be caught or arrested
Dover is the Kent ferry port
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bird captured once the boat had cleared harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is the English Channel port facing France; taking R from it leaves the second word of the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The collared dove is a common grey-brown bird with a black neck band, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Remedies involved sedation with bit of treatment internally

indicators.note: involved means tangled and complicated, so the letters of the next word are twisted
only a small bit of the word is wanted, its first letter
internally says this piece goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of treatment

explanation.surface: Cures that used sedation alongside a little treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Antidotes are medicines that counteract poisons, so they are remedies in a medical sense.

clue.text: Piece of chicken from hob's cooked in port, perhaps

indicators.note: cooked food is altered from its raw state, so the letters are reworked
in says one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: port is an example of a fortified wine, flagged by 'perhaps'
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A chicken bone from a dish cooked on the hob in port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests a harbour, but 'perhaps' marks it as an example of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The wishbone is the forked bone between a chicken's neck and breast, a part of the bird.

clue.text: Dictionary in a judge's room

blocks.note: first meaning: the ... dictionary, a British reference favoured by crossword setters
second meaning: a judge's private rooms where cases are heard out of open court

explanation.surface: A dictionary lying in a judge's private office.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers is a well-known British dictionary publisher, and a judge's private office is called chambers.

clue.text: Make unexpected fortune out of industrial action — it's preposterous

blocks.note: a strike is workers' industrial action
taken as written
as in 'that's rich!', said of something outrageous

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fortune from a walkout, which seems absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike it rich is an idiom for suddenly gaining great wealth, as a prospector hitting gold.

clue.text: A provision of meals on base

blocks.note: taken as written
board is food provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Meals are provided at a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On base' suggests a military camp, but it is the baseball sense of a runner standing on a base.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball, a runner who is aboard has reached base safely, so aboard means on base.

clue.text: This shopkeeper's poor, or is he?

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters that follow are in disarray

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a certain shopkeeper is really as poor as claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like a description of the shopkeeper, but it signals the rearrangement of the three words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosier is a merchant who sells stockings, socks and similar knitted goods.

clue.text: Liberal, outspoken, objected

blocks.note: broad can mean plain-spoken or blunt, as in broad humour
to have minded something is to have objected to it

explanation.surface: A liberal who spoke frankly and raised objections.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad-minded means tolerant of other views, which is the sense of liberal as an adjective.

clue.text: Poke one with end of first finger

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is used

blocks.note: a dig is a poke or prod
I is the Roman numeral for one
the final letter of first

explanation.surface: Prod someone with the tip of your index finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First finger' reads as the index finger, but 'first' is only there to supply its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Digit is the anatomical word for a finger or toe.

clue.text: Licensed amateur radio operator in Champigny-sur-Marne

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the place name that follows

blocks.note: letters two to four of the town's name

explanation.surface: A radio enthusiast based in a town near Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Champigny-sur-Marne is a suburb east of Paris; the answer sits right at its start.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is the informal term for a licensed amateur radio operator.

clue.text: Emerge carrying infant close to cardinal and philosopher

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted
to carry something is to hold it within, so the first word wraps what follows

blocks.note: to arise is to emerge
a tot is a small child
the final letter of cardinal

explanation.surface: A cardinal and a philosopher appear, someone carrying a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato, so he is an example of a philosopher.

clue.text: Good to wander through small wooded area

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: It is pleasant to stroll through a small wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Through' looks like an insertion signal, but nothing goes inside anything: it simply links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grove is a small group of trees, a little wood or orchard.

clue.text: Thirsty, drinking rosé? I suspect that's ridiculously inadequate

indicators.note: one who drinks takes a thing inside, so the first word holds the rest
suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters before it are not in their proper order

blocks.note: dry can mean thirsty
taken as written, accent dropped

explanation.surface: A thirsty drinker suspects the measure of rosé they were served is pitifully small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' reads as the speaker's aside, but 'I' belongs to the fodder and 'suspect' alone signals the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means so small or poor as to be laughable, such as a derisory pay offer.

clue.text: Force second lock

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Applying force to a secondary lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door, but here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, stress is the force acting on a material, so the noun matches force.
